feature: Card back: Common Confusions, Synonyms, Antonyms (scorecard row 13-14)
why_not_way_better: Their card back shows lookalikes (illusory: illusion, illustrate, elusive), synonyms and antonyms. Ours has only about 80 lookalike pairs (override 15, words.md:1200) for about 1,080 SAT headwords. That covers about 160 words, so more than 85% of entries get no NOT THE SAME AS row. The build checks (rebuild-v2.md:9398, and override 17 at words.md:1212) never require `same`, `opposite` or a confusion on an entry. That breaks review change 1's promise that 'every entry has... synonyms, antonyms and lookalikes' (rebuild-v2.md:9222). W1's `lookalike` trap and W9's Fix-card fallback ('else its top lookalike') depend on this data too. So for most words ours shows less than theirs, and row 14's 'WAY BETTER already' holds only for about 160 words.
fix: Add a `lookalikes` field to every SAT entry: 1-3 slugs or plain words, each with a one-line tell. Or grow confusions.json until every SAT sense has at least one lookalike or sense confusion (about 600 or more). Add build checks: every SAT sense has at least 1 confusion with a tell, at least 2 `same`, and at least 1 `opposite` (or an explicit `no_opposite: true`). Acceptance: GET /api/words/{slug} for 50 random SAT slugs returns non-empty confusions, same and opposite.

feature: Plan Vocabulary/Flashcards tasks and the Today Words tile launch buttons (row 32, W11, overrides 6/42/43)
why_not_way_better: W11 (words.md:717-718) and overrides 6, 42 and 43 put Review cards, Learn 10 and Quiz in a hidden ⋯ menu on the Today tile and the Plan task, leaving one primary button. Theirs has direct launch buttons (Study words / Review cards). The v2 spec and plan.md L4 (plan.md:381) showed all three. Folding one-tap actions into a menu is what decision 4 forbids: things are never 'collapsed away or hidden', and 'one-tap ways to the next step' belong.
fix: Keep Today's words as the pill. Show Review cards (N due) · Learn 10 · Quiz as visible quiet buttons beside it on the Today tile, the Plan Words task and the phone menu row. The ⋯ menu holds only Mark done / Skip / Undo. Update W11's Entry bullets, overrides 6, 42 and 43, and the plan.md L4 and S3 rows in §3.2. Acceptance: the Today Words tile shows 4 buttons with no menu open.

feature: Right-answer feedback in quizzes (row 24, W1 and W11 auto-advance)
why_not_way_better: A right quiz answer moves on after 700 ms by default (`prefs.words_autonext` on, words.md:211 and :731). The clue and all four reasons 'show' for 0.7 s, too short to read, so on every right answer the reasons are in effect hidden, lucky guesses included. The only hold is 'any key, or the pointer over the verdict', and neither exists on a phone. This goes against decision 4, and against today.md T14, which removed v2's hide-after-right-answer for that reason. Theirs waits for Next, so their student can at least look. Ours shows more, then takes it away.
fix: Turn `words_autonext` off by default in quiz, Today's words and Words check runs; keep it on only in Sprint (W16). When a student turns it on, wait at least 2.5 s with a visible draining ring. On touch, a pointerdown anywhere on the verdict holds it. Never auto-advance after a right answer marked `conf:'guess'` or answered in under 3 s. Add a browser acceptance check at 390 px with touch emulation.

feature: Word of the day / Transition of the day (W21) against Today T14
why_not_way_better: W21 is out of date with today.md T14. W21 says Transition of the day appears 'on /words/ only' and has no record-once rule. But T14 puts the same `words.daily_item(day,'transition')` item in Today's `rw:transition` slot. A student can answer it on /words/, see the key, then answer again on Today, which spoils T14's crowd split, streak and key hiding. The two files also give two formulas for one function. W21 draws the WIC word from `daily.word(day,'sat')` (sha256 'word:sat:{day}'); T14 draws it from sha256('qotd:rw:wic:'+day) over words with at least 2 frames. The words.md header still says 'Today's third slot', but T14 now has four slots.
fix: Rewrite W21 so both daily items are T14's `rw:wic` and `rw:transition` slots. Each is recorded once through `words.record_daily(learner, day, fmt, ...)` in session `qotd:rw:{fmt}:{day}`, and shows as answered on both pages. Define one hash, T14's, and only inside `words.daily_item`. Acceptance: answering the transition on /words/ makes GET /api/qotd show `rw:transition` answered, and a second POST from Today returns the first answer.

feature: Library tile to flashcard (row 10, W14 covered sheet)
why_not_way_better: (a) It can't be built as written. W14 files Know / Don't know from the sheet 'as a card review under §12' but names no endpoint: run answers need a run id, and sheet samples need an HMAC token. It also doesn't say how W7's box-0 rules apply outside a run. (b) With Meanings off, which is the default, MEANING 'and everything below' is hidden: YOUR RECORD, the journey, the SAT-style sample, shades and confusions. That happens even when the student searched for a word just to look it up. The most common Library action gets slower, and useful panels are hidden (decision 4).
fix: Add `POST /api/words/{slug}/grade {ok, ms}`. It files one word_reviews row (mode 'sheet', kind 'card') under W7: a box-0 Know goes to box 2, a self-grade never lifts a word above box 3, and an early review doesn't promote. Cover only the blocks that give the answer away (MEANING, examples, new sentence, same/opposite, shades); keep chips, YOUR RECORD and the journey visible. Open the sheet uncovered when the student arrives with a search `q`, from a gloss popover, or from Open word. Put a Covered / Open toggle in the sheet head, remembered in localStorage.

feature: Supply of Words in Context and Transitions items (rows 12, 21, 36, 37; W1, W2, W8)
why_not_way_better: 'Unlimited, never repeats' rests on about 300 frames (at least 2 per class) and about 40 transition families (at least 5 second-sentence variants each). The slots only swap names, fields and sites. The build minimum lets a sense be a legal key in just 2 frames. So W8's 'fresh sentence on every review' alternates between 2 texts, and 'Same word, new text' runs dry after one press. That is about 300 distinct WIC texts and about 200 transition texts, roughly the size of their fixed 363 WIC and 204 Transitions QBank items, and theirs include real College Board passages. There is no rule against serving a learner a frame they've already seen. The rejection of `ctx_seen` (words.md:1681) assumes 'the frame generator gives unlimited contexts per sense', which is false at 2 frames. The SAT's literary-excerpt WIC items (narration, older register) are not covered at all.
fix: Raise the minimums: at least 6 legal frames per SAT sense across at least 2 of the 3 subjects (a build check), about 1,500 frames in total, and at least 150 transition families (at least 15 per logic). Add fixed frames made from public-domain literary excerpts (pre-1929 texts) with need tags, at least 20% of the literature subject. The generator should pick frames this learner hasn't seen (from word_reviews.template) before repeating any, and W8's sentence should do the same. Acceptance: 30 calls in a row of `another(like='word')` on a core word return at least 6 distinct templates, and a 200-item run for one learner repeats no template until every eligible one has been used.

feature: Single defensible key and self-policing distractors (rows 22 and 26; W1, W18)
why_not_way_better: W1's 'one defensible key' depends entirely on hand-tagged features (class, polarity, intensity 1-5, pattern) for about 1,180 senses. The verifier checks them against themselves (its ponytail note says so). The content review is an open question with no owner and no gate (§3.8.9, override 54). One wrong intensity tag makes a 'too strong' distractor a legal key, which is exactly their ingenious / imaginative / innovative / original bug. W18's auto-guard needs 20 or more first tries from learners with 80%+ accuracy per (frame, distractor) pair, which a new site won't reach for most pairs. Only the 3-report path would actually fire. Nothing buildable guarantees that we can't ship their bug.
fix: Add a required review gate. `tools/build_words.py --review` prints each frame × legal key's full items (5 seeds). A frame is served only once `reviewed: {by, date}` is set in frames.json, and the build fails on a served frame without it. Two independent adjudications per item (human or scripted model) answer 'does exactly one option fit?', and a disagreement blocks the frame. Lower the auto-guard to 2 reports, or 40% or more of at least 8 strong-learner first tries, and pull the frame for review when it trips.

why_not_way_better: Measured difficulty appears only after 20 first-try in-context answers across learners on a word as key. With about 1,180 senses on a new site, almost every tile will show the authored 'est.' level for months, which is the same authored guess theirs uses. The Easy / Medium / Hard filter itself is theirs. 'WAY BETTER' depends on traffic the site won't have at launch.
fix: Blend from the first answer: show p = (right + 20·prior)/(n + 20), where the prior comes from the authored level (easy .8, medium .6, hard .4), with 'n answers' beside it. Base the prior on an objective signal stored per entry at build time (a frequency band from a public word-frequency list, plus `value`), not the author's guess alone. Make 'Hard for you' a Difficulty filter value, not only a sort, so the personal axis filters from day one.

feature: Placement: skip what you already know (rows 3 and 33, W10)
why_not_way_better: Placement tests 48 real words, yet its result promises 'The 190 you said you know come back once each' (words.md:648-649), which 48 items can't produce. The New deck 'skips bands estimated at 90% or more' (words.md:653), which leaves those words at box 0 forever: never taught, never proven, never Known, and never clearly counted in By exam day's 'left'. The roughly 10% of a skipped band the student doesn't know never comes up. It can't be built as written.
fix: Say that only the 48 placement words go to box 3 / Claimed. Words in bands estimated at 90% or more get `placed=2`, 'Probably known', and enter Today's words as one in-context proof each, 1-2 a day spread before the exam. A right proof makes the word Known; a wrong one puts it at the front of New. Add a 'Confirm the rest · N words · ~3 min' triage chip on the result. Fix the copy so it counts placement plus triage words.

why_not_way_better: Generated R&W answers live only in word_reviews, read by Words-only code (W5 insights, W13 journey, W18 crowd, T14 streak), outside attempts. When the R&W bank lands, its WIC and Transitions results will go into attempts. Months of Words answers will then either stay invisible to R&W mastery and the estimate, or need a migration and a rewrite of those readers. That goes against decision 3, and nothing supports the 'without a rewrite' claim (words.md:21-22).
fix: Store `subject:'rw'`, `skill` ('Words in Context' | 'Transitions') and the College Board domain on every generated word_reviews row now. Send every read through one accessor, `words.rw_answers(learner, since)`. Write the migration now: one INSERT…SELECT mapping word_reviews (template, seed, given, correct, ms, session, at) into attempts with subject='rw'. Add a test_flow check that the mapping covers every column the attempts consumers read.

feature: Bring your words: paste a text (row 30, W19)
why_not_way_better: 'Not in the library' offers words of 7 or more letters that are 'not in the library or the common-word list', matched in the browser. That common-word list is never named, sized, shipped or served, so the feature can't be built as written. Without it, every long ordinary word gets offered as a new own word.
fix: Ship `server/words/common.json`: the top 10,000 English words from a public-domain frequency list, with inflections. Serve it with /api/words/index (ETag, max-age). Acceptance: pasting 'The researchers' measurements demonstrated ...' offers no common word under Not in the library.

why_not_way_better: 'W shows the first letter', but in Type it the focus is in the text field, and §2.8 ignores every key there except Enter and Esc. No hint button is specified, so as written the hint can't be reached.
fix: Add a visible 'Hint · first letter' button next to the field, bound to Alt+W, which §2.8 should allow inside that field. Using it marks the answer hinted (right, but no promotion).
